headline_seed: Middle East crisis live: Iran ‘offers to end chokehold on strait of Hormuz’
description_seed: Sources say country wants US to end its blockade as part of proposal but has not addressed its nuclear programme Iran is offering to end its chokehold on the strait of Hormuz without addressing its nuclear program, two regional officials with knowledge of the proposal said Monday. It comes as the country’s foreign minister made a visit to Russia he said was an opportunity to consult with Moscow regarding the war against Israel and the United States. Continue reading...
Iran is offering to end its chokehold on the strait of Hormuz without addressing its nuclear program, two regional officials with knowledge of the proposal said Monday.
It comes as the country’s foreign minister made a visit to Russia he said was an opportunity to consult with Moscow regarding the war against Israel and the United States.

A day after round 2 of the US and Iran peace talks failed to take off in Islamabad, Pakistan mediators are trying to revive the mediation efforts. On Saturday, April 25, Iran's foreign minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi had left Islamabad without waiting for US envoys. Trump had also cancelled the scheduled visit of his officials saying Washington was having all the cards and added that if Tehran wants, it can call them (US) at any time. Iran conveyed to Pakistan that they will not participate in any direct or indirect talks until US lifts Strait of Hormuz blockade.
